name: Alcohol poisoning
description: Alcohol poisoning can happen when you drink alcohol quicker than your body can process it. It can make you seriously ill and you may need to go to hospital for treatment.
symptom_terms: slurring words or being unable to speak
being unable to coordinate movement – for example, being unable to stand, walk, or pick things up

care_notes: You'll need to go to hospital to be monitored if you have alcohol poisoning. It can cause serious complications, like liver and heart failure, which can be fatal.
You may be given fluids, which may be given into your veins with a drip.

symptom_terms: pain or discomfort in the upper right side of your tummy (abdomen)
yellowing of the skin or whites of the eyes (jaundice) – yellowing of the skin may be harder to see on black or brown skin

blood in your vomit or poo (poo may look black, vomit may look like coffee grounds)
problems with confusion, concentration and memory
care_notes: Get medical help if you think you might have alcohol-related liver disease (ARLD). Do not wait for symptoms to get worse.
The aim of treatment for alcohol-related liver disease (ARLD) is usually to help you stop drinking alcohol completely. This is important whatever stage of ARLD you have.

name: Bronchiectasis
description: Bronchiectasis is a condition where the airways in your lungs are damaged and produce a lot of phlegm (mucus). It cannot usually be cured, but treatment can help manage it.
symptom_terms: a cough that does not go away
coughing up a lot of phlegm (mucus) – the phlegm may be clear, white, yellow or green
getting frequent chest infections, where your symptoms get worse for a few days or weeks and you may feel generally unwell

care_notes: Bronchiectasis cannot usually be cured. The aim of treatment is to manage your symptoms and help stop them getting worse.

symptom_terms: an ache or pain in your fingers, hand or arm
a weak thumb or difficulty gripping
care_notes: Carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) sometimes gets better by itself in a few months, particularly if you have it because you're pregnant.

symptom_terms: your eyes being uncomfortable in, or sensitive to, light and glare
looking at 1 object but seeing 2 (double vision)
care_notes: Cataracts do not usually need treatment straight away.

symptom_terms: a constantly blocked or runny nose
feeling like there's a lump or something stuck in your throat
a frequent need to swallow or cough to try to clear your throat
a feeling that mucus is slowly dripping down the back of your throat (postnasal drip)
a crackling feeling in your ears
care_notes: Although catarrh can be annoying, phlegm and mucus are not harmful and are the body's way of clearing infection.

care_notes: If you have a chest infection, there are things you can do to ease the symptoms.

ear infections that keep coming back

has difficulty with tasks involving sorting colours
care_notes: There is currently no treatment for colour vision deficiency that runs in families. Most people adapt to seeing colours differently.

a feeling of pressure in your ears and face
care_notes: You can usually treat a cold at home without seeing a GP.

symptom_terms: severe pain in a muscle – the pain may be worse when stretching it
numbness, weakness or pins and needles
tightness or difficulty moving the affected body part
care_notes: Treatment for compartment syndrome depends on whether it happens suddenly or comes on gradually.

symptom_terms: being slow in putting on weight and growing
swelling around the tummy and swollen hands, ankles and feet
being sweatier than usual, but skin feels cool and clammy
heart palpitations - when your heartbeat feels uncomfortable or unusual
care_notes: You need to get medical help immediately if you think you or your child have symptoms of congenital heart disease.
If you or your child are diagnosed with congenital heart disease, you’ll be referred to a specialist team at an NHS hospital.

the poo is unusually large or small and is dry, hard or lumpy
you are straining or in pain when you have a poo
you feel like you haven't fully emptied your bowels
care_notes: Making simple changes to your diet and lifestyle can help treat constipation.
It's safe to try these simple measures when you're pregnant.

It's important to get chest pain checked to rule out other, more serious conditions.

remember to take any medicine you've been prescribed

symptom_terms: a cough that does not go away and brings up mucus
frequent sinus infections (sinusitis) and chest infections
large, greasy and sticky poos that are hard to flush away

few or no tears when they cry

care_notes: You may need medical help if you get ill after travelling somewhere where there’s a risk of dengue.

symptom_terms: intense toothache or pain in your gums
redness inside the mouth, or outside the mouth on the face or jaw
sensitivity to hot or cold food and drink in the affected area
a bad taste in your mouth
difficulty opening your mouth and chewing food
swollen glands on each side of your neck

a dark "curtain" or shadow in your vision
changes to your eyesight, such as blurred vision

one leg moves differently to the other during things like play and nappy changes

breath that smells fruity (like pear drop sweets or nail polish remover)

finding it harder to see in the dark or low light

description: Hepatitis is when your liver becomes inflamed, usually due to a virus or drinking too much alcohol over a long period of time. Some types of hepatitis can lead to serious problems if not treated.
symptom_terms: yellowing of your skin and the whites of your eyes ( jaundice ) – yellowed skin may be less noticeable if you have brown or black skin
pain in your upper tummy, usually under the right side of your ribs
feeling or being sick (nausea or vomiting)
care_notes: How hepatitis is treated depends on the type, what's caused it or how serious it is.
Some types, such as hepatitis A and hepatitis E, usually get better without treatment for the virus.

name: Hepatitis A
description: Hepatitis A is a liver infection that is spread in the poo of an infected person. Most people who get it get better within a few months.
symptom_terms: flu-like symptoms, such as tiredness, headache, and muscle pains
pale yellow or pale grey poo
itchy skin – you may also have a raised rash ( hives )
yellowing of the skin and the whites of the eyes ( jaundice ) - this may be harder to see on brown and black skin
care_notes: You think you might have hepatitis A and:
Hepatitis A usually clears up on its own within 3 to 6 months.

name: Hepatitis B
description: Hepatitis B is a liver infection spread through blood and body fluids. You can be vaccinated against hepatitis B and the chance of getting it in the UK is low. The infection usually only lasts for a few months, but some people can have it long term.
symptom_terms: a raised rash that may be itchy ( hives )
yellowing of the skin and whites of the eyes ( jaundice ) – yellowed skin may be less noticeable on brown or black skin
care_notes: Hepatitis B usually clears up on its own without treatment. You may be offered medicine to help with the symptoms, such as painkillers or medicines to stop you feeling sick.
Your GP will refer you to see a liver specialist who will check how well your liver is working.

name: Hepatitis C
description: Hepatitis C is a virus spread through contact with infected blood. Many people have no symptoms, but if it's not treated it can cause serious damage to the liver. Treatment cures the infection for most people.
symptom_terms: yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes ( jaundice ) – this may be harder to see on black or brown skin
care_notes: Treatment can cure hepatitis C infections in most people.
If you're diagnosed with hepatitis C, you'll usually be referred to a specialist for treatment.

care_notes: Osteomyelitis is treated with antibiotics. You may need treatment in hospital, or you might be able to take antibiotics at home.

name: Overview - Brain abscess
description: A brain abscess is a pus-filled swelling in the brain. It usually occurs when bacteria or fungi enter the brain tissue after an infection or severe head injury.
symptom_terms: headache – which is often severe, located in a single section of the head and cannot be relieved with painkillers
changes in mental state – such as confusion or irritability

care_notes: A brain abscess is regarded as a medical emergency. Swelling caused by the abscess can disrupt the blood and oxygen supply to the brain. There's also a risk of the abscess bursting (rupturing).

name: Overview - Transient ischaemic attack (TIA)
description: A transient ischaemic attack (TIA) or "mini stroke" is caused by a temporary disruption in the blood supply to part of the brain.
symptom_terms: Face – the face may have dropped on 1 side, the person may not be able to smile, or their mouth or eye may have dropped.
Arms – the person may not be able to lift both arms and keep them raised because of weakness or numbness in 1 arm.
care_notes: Although the symptoms of a transient ischaemic attack (TIA) resolve in a few minutes or hours, you'll need treatment to help prevent another TIA or a full stroke happening in the future.
Treatment will depend on your individual circumstances, such as your age and medical history.

name: Overview - Trigeminal neuralgia
description: Trigeminal neuralgia is sudden, severe facial pain. It's often described as a sharp shooting pain or like having an electric shock in the jaw, teeth or gums.
symptom_terms: a cool breeze or air conditioning
vibrations, such as walking or travelling in a car
care_notes: Trigeminal neuralgia is usually a long-term condition and the periods of remission often get shorter over time. However, the treatments available do help most cases to some degree.

An anticonvulsant medicine called carbamazepine , which is often used to treat epilepsy , is the first treatment usually recommended to treat trigeminal neuralgia. Carbamazepine can relieve nerve pain by slowing down electrical impulses in the nerves and reducing their ability to transmit pain messages.

symptom_terms: changes to your mood, personality or behaviour
symptoms of Alzheimer's disease , such as problems with memory and language (many people with vascular dementia also have Alzheimer's disease)
care_notes: There's currently no cure for vascular dementia and there's no way to reverse any loss of brain cells that happened before the condition was diagnosed.

care_notes: Most venous leg ulcers heal within 6 months if they're treated by a healthcare professional trained in compression therapy for leg ulcers.
But some ulcers may take longer to heal, and a very small number never heal.

problems with memory, understanding and judgement
care_notes: Most cases of vitamin B12 and folate deficiency can be easily treated with injections or tablets to replace the missing vitamins.
Vitamin B12 supplements are usually given by injection at first.

The white patches caused by vitiligo are usually permanent, although treatment options are available to reduce their appearance.

care_notes: Tell anyone you speak to about your recent travel, and if you were bitten by a mosquito or might have been.
If you become unwell while you're abroad, get medical help as soon as possible. Do not wait until you get back to the UK.

care_notes: There's no specific treatment for Patau's syndrome. As a result of the severe health problems a newborn baby with the syndrome will have, doctors usually focus on minimising discomfort and ensuring the baby is able to feed.

name: Pelvic inflammatory disease
description: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) is an infection that affects a woman's womb, fallopian tubes and ovaries. It can affect anyone with a womb. If it's diagnosed early, it can be easily treated with antibiotics.
symptom_terms: pain in the area between your tummy and thighs (pelvic pain) or in your lower tummy

heavy or painful periods that are unusual for you
bleeding between periods or after sex
vaginal discharge that looks, smells or feels unusual for you
care_notes: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) is usually easy to treat if it's diagnosed early. If it's left untreated or the infection is severe, you may need to go to hospital.
The main treatment is antibiotics. The doctor will usually give you an injection of antibiotics, and prescribe antibiotic tablets for you to take for 2 weeks.

If you do not have any symptoms, or the prolapse is not bothering you, you may not need medical treatment.

name: Polymorphic light eruption
description: Polymorphic light eruption (also called polymorphous light eruption) is a skin rash that can happen after being in the sun. It usually goes away on its own if you stay out of the sun, but it can keep coming back.
symptom_terms: have small raised spots or blisters
be itchy or feel like it's burning
be red or pink – this may be harder to see on brown or black skin
care_notes: The polymorphic light eruption rash usually goes away in around 1 week if you avoid being in the sun. It can last longer or get worse if you continue to go in the sun.
The rash may also come back when your skin is exposed to sunlight again.

care_notes: Get medical help if you think you have pompholyx or you have any changes to your skin you’re worried about.
Pompholyx is usually a long-term condition that comes and goes over time. Treatment can help control the symptoms.

loss of feeling in your skin
care_notes: Post-herpetic neuralgia can be difficult to treat. It usually gets better eventually, but how long this takes can vary from a few months to over a year.

symptom_terms: problems with your stomach or digestion, such as feeling sick, being sick, diarrhoea, constipation, bloating and tummy pain
headaches and problems with your sight, such as blurred vision or tunnel vision

weakness and extreme tiredness (fatigue), not being able to do much exercise, and sleeping badly
problems with thinking, memory and concentration (brain fog)
care_notes: If you have symptoms of postural tachycardia syndrome (PoTS), it's important to get them checked out.
If you're diagnosed with postural tachycardia syndrome (PoTS), finding the right treatment for you can take time.

recognising other things, such as cars or animals

symptom_terms: pain when peeing, which may feel like stinging or burning

needing to pee more often than usual
pain in your penis, scrotum, testicles or bottom
care_notes: Prostatitis is treated with antibiotics . You'll usually feel better within 2 weeks after starting treatment, but it may take several weeks for all your symptoms to get better.
If you've had symptoms of prostatitis for 3 months or longer (chronic prostatitis) you may be referred to a specialist (a urologist).

name: Pubic lice
description: Pubic lice (sometimes called crabs) are tiny insects that can live on body hair, especially the pubic hair around the penis or vagina. They're spread through close body contact, most commonly through sexual contact.
symptom_terms: itching, which is usually worse at night
small red or blue spots on your skin (lice bites)
white or yellow dots attached to your hair (lice eggs)
dark red or brown spots in your underwear (lice poo)
care_notes: The main treatments for pubic lice are medicated creams or shampoos that kill the lice.

You usually need to use the treatment on your whole body (but not on your eyebrows or eyelashes) and leave it on for 12 hours or overnight before washing it off. You'll need to repeat this again a week later to make sure all the lice have been killed.

chest pain that's worse when you breathe in
care_notes: If a GP thinks you've got a pulmonary embolism, you'll be sent to hospital for further tests and treatment.
At hospital, you'll probably be given an injection of anticoagulant medicine before you get any test results.

care_notes: There are a number of things you can do to help ease the symptoms of repetitive strain injury (RSI).

faster breathing or long gaps between breaths
difficulty feeding (in babies) or loss of appetite
care_notes: There's no specific treatment for an RSV infection.

care_notes: Most respiratory tract infections (RTIs) pass within 1 to 2 weeks. You can usually treat your symptoms at home.
A pharmacist can suggest treatments to help relieve your symptoms, such as decongestants and nasal sprays.

uncomfortable feelings in your legs, such as tingling, throbbing or itching

name: Rickets and osteomalacia
description: Rickets is where a child's bones become weak and soft. It's usually caused by not getting enough vitamin D or calcium. In adults it's called osteomalacia. Treatment and lifestyle changes can help.
symptom_terms: pain in your back, shoulder, ribs, pelvis or legs
changes in the way you walk, not wanting to walk much or getting tired more easily when walking

tingling, cramping or twitching of your muscles

care_notes: Rickets and osteomalacia are usually caused by low levels of vitamin D and calcium in your body.
Our bodies make vitamin D when our skin is exposed to summer sunlight. But we cannot make enough vitamin D from sunlight between September and March, which can cause low vitamin D levels.

care_notes: If your episodes of supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) only last a few minutes and do not bother you, you may not need treatment.

name: Syphilis
description: Syphilis is a sexually transmitted infection (STI). If it's not treated, it can cause serious and potentially life-threatening problems.
symptom_terms: small sores (ulcers) on your penis, vagina, or around your bottom (anus) – these are usually painless and you may only have one of them
sores in other areas, including in your mouth or on your lips, hands or bottom
white or grey warty growths most commonly on your penis, vagina or around your anus
a rash on the palms of your hands and soles of your feet that can sometimes spread all over your body – this is not usually itchy
flu-like symptoms, such as a high temperature, headaches and tiredness
patchy hair loss on the head, beard and eyebrows
care_notes: Syphilis is treated with antibiotics , which you may have as injections, tablets or capsules.
Treatment may be started before your test result is known. How long you need treatment for will depend on the stage of your syphilis.

description: Tailbone pain is pain in the bone at the base of the spine (coccyx), near the top of your bottom. There are things you can do to ease the pain, but get medical help if it does not get better after a few weeks.
symptom_terms: when you sit down or stand up
care_notes: In many areas you may be able to get help, such as physiotherapy, from NHS community musculoskeletal (MSK) services without needing a referral from a GP.

name: Temporal arteritis
description: Temporal arteritis (giant cell arteritis) is where the arteries, particularly those at the side of the head (the temples), become inflamed. It's serious and needs urgent treatment.
symptom_terms: pain or tenderness at the side of your head (temples) or on the scalp
jaw pain while eating or talking
vision problems, such as double vision or loss of vision in 1 or both eyes
care_notes: It can lead to serious problems like stroke and blindness if not treated quickly.
Temporal arteritis is treated with steroid medicine , usually prednisolone .

clicking, popping or grinding noises when you move your jaw
your jaw locking when you open your mouth

symptom_terms: pain in a tendon that gets worse when you move
feeling a grating or crackling sensation when you move the tendon
swelling, sometimes with heat or redness
care_notes: Follow these steps for 2 to 3 days to help manage pain and support the tendon.
It's important to take a bandage or brace off before going to bed.

name: Tennis elbow

symptom_terms: tenderness or swelling in your elbow
care_notes: There are a number of things you can do to help ease the symptoms of tennis elbow.
In many areas you may be able to get help, such as physiotherapy, from NHS community musculoskeletal (MSK) services without needing a referral from a GP.

the affected area may feel tender and your head may hurt more when touched

the affected arm gets tired easily
pain and swelling in the affected arm
the affected hand and arm feels cold
the skin on the hand turns blue, grey or pale – this can be harder to see on brown or black skin

name: Threadworms
description: Threadworms (pinworms) are tiny worms in your poo. They're common in children and spread easily. You can treat them without seeing a GP.
symptom_terms: extreme itching around the anus or vagina, particularly at night
irritability and waking up during the night
care_notes: You can buy a medicine called mebendazole for threadworms from pharmacies. This is usually a chewable tablet or liquid you swallow.
Treat everyone aged 2 years and over in your household, even if they do not have symptoms.

name: Thrombophilia
description: Thrombophilia is a condition where your blood clots more easily. It can usually be treated with medicines that help prevent blood clots.
symptom_terms: throbbing pain and swelling in your legs and arms ( deep vein thrombosis )
sudden breathing difficulties, chest pain and coughing up blood ( pulmonary embolism )
care_notes: These could be the symptoms of a blood clot in your leg or your lungs.
You may get pain and swelling in your arm or tummy instead if that's where the blood clot is.

name: Thrush in men and women
description: Thrush is a common yeast infection that affects men and women. It's usually harmless but it can be uncomfortable and keep coming back. It is not classed as a sexually transmitted infection (STI).
symptom_terms: white vaginal discharge (often like cottage cheese), which does not usually smell
itching and irritation around the vulva and vagina
soreness and stinging during sex or when you pee
irritation, burning and redness around the head of the penis and under the foreskin
care_notes: You'll usually need antifungal medicine to get rid of thrush. This can be a tablet you take, a tablet you insert into your vagina (pessary) or a cream to relieve the irritation.
Thrush should clear up within 7 to 14 days of starting treatment.

pain in the front of your neck, or a feeling like something is pressing against your neck
a red face (flushing) – this may be harder to see on brown or black skin

a stiff neck and a severe headache
pain when looking at bright lights
a change in behaviour, confusion or slurred speech

pus-filled spots or white patches on your tonsils

symptom_terms: sharp pain in your tooth when eating or drinking hot, cold or sweet things (sensitive teeth)
white, brown or black spots on your tooth
care_notes: Treatment for tooth decay depends on how severe it is.
A dentist can prescribe fluoride treatments like mouthwash or varnish to reverse early tooth decay.

a raised skin rash that feels like sandpaper

care_notes: If you're pregnant, you can also call your midwife for advice.

name: Trichomoniasis
description: Trichomoniasis, sometimes called trich, is a sexually transmitted infection (STI) passed on though vaginal sex or sharing sex toys. It can cause serious problems if it's not treated.
symptom_terms: yellow-green discharge from your vagina – this may look frothy or smell like fish
itching, pain, soreness, swelling or redness in or around your vagina
pain when peeing or having vaginal sex
pain or soreness in your penis, testicles (balls) or bottom, or when you ejaculate
care_notes: Trichomoniasis is treated with antibiotics, usually metronidazole . You'll take it either twice a day for 7 days or as a one-off dose.
If you have symptoms, they should start to get better within a few days of starting the antibiotics. It's important to finish the course of antibiotics even if you start to feel better.

stiffness in the affected finger or thumb
needing to put pressure on the affected finger or thumb to straighten it from a bent position
care_notes: Trigger finger can sometimes get better on its own without any treatment.

name: Tuberculosis (TB)
description: Tuberculosis (TB) is an infection that usually affects the lungs. It can be treated with antibiotics but can be serious if not treated. There's a vaccine that helps protect some people who are at risk from TB.
symptom_terms: a cough that lasts more than 3 weeks – you may cough up mucus (phlegm) or mucus with blood in it
a high temperature or night sweats
not feeling as hungry as usual (loss of appetite)
a rash on the legs, face or other part of the body
care_notes: If you have symptoms of tuberculosis, it’s important to get them checked.
The main treatment for tuberculosis (TB) is to take antibiotics, usually for at least 6 months.

name: Turner syndrome

symptom_terms: be born smaller than usual and grow up to be shorter than average
have underdeveloped ovaries, which can affect puberty and cause infertility
care_notes: There is currently no cure for Turner syndrome, but there are treatments and support to help children and adults have the best possible quality of life.

A range of health professionals may be involved in your or your child's care. They'll help to create a care plan and advise you about which treatments may be needed, depending on your or your child's symptoms.

feeling very thirsty and drinking more than usual
losing weight without trying to or looking thinner
breath that smells sweet or fruity (like nail polish remover or pear drop sweets)
cuts and wounds taking longer to heal

description: Typhoid fever is an infection spread through unclean food or water. It can cause serious problems if not treated. You should have a typhoid vaccination if you're travelling to an area where there's a risk of getting it.
symptom_terms: high temperature, which may slowly get worse over a few days
not pooing as often as normal or finding it hard to poo (constipation)
care_notes: Tell anyone you speak to about your recent travel.
If you're still abroad, get medical help where you are as soon as possible. Do not wait until you get back to the UK.

symptom_terms: a rash, which may be harder to see on black or brown skin
care_notes: If a doctor thinks you could have typhus, they'll usually suggest a blood test or skin biopsy .
Antibiotics are used to treat a typhus infection. They're usually started before you get your test result, as this can take up to a week.

tummy pain, particularly in the lower-left part of your tummy – this may get better after pooing
needing to poo frequently, urgently or during the night
feeling like you need to poo even though your bowel is empty
farting a lot or feeling bloated

name: Umbilical hernia
description: An umbilical hernia is a bulge in the tummy caused by part of the bowel, or surrounding fat, pushing through a weakness in the muscles.
care_notes: Children do not usually need treatment for an umbilical hernia as the hernia will usually disappear by the time they're 5 years old.
Treatment is usually only needed if the hernia is very big or does not disappear.

name: Underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism)
description: An underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism) is a common condition where the thyroid gland in your neck does not make enough hormones. This can cause symptoms like tiredness and weight gain. It can be managed with treatment.
symptom_terms: dry skin, dry hair or hair loss
irregular or heavy periods if you have them
care_notes: An underactive thyroid is usually treated with medicine to replace the thyroid hormone that your body cannot produce. This medicine is usually levothyroxine tablets.
You'll usually need to take them for the rest of your life to prevent your symptoms returning. You should be able to live a normal life.

care_notes: Undescended testicles often move into their usual place in the scrotum in the first 12 weeks after your child is born.

symptom_terms: pain or a burning feeling when you pee
white or cloudy discharge from the vagina or penis
an irritated or sore tip of the penis
care_notes: Urethritis is usually treated with antibiotics. It may take a week or two for your symptoms to disappear completely.
Any current sexual partners may also need treatment.

needing to pee more often than usual
needing to pee more often than usual during the night (nocturia)
needing to pee suddenly or more urgently than usual
lower tummy pain or pain in your back, just under the ribs
a high temperature, or feeling hot or cold, and shivery
have a high temperature – your child is feeling hotter than usual if you touch their neck, back or tummy
appear generally unwell – babies and young children may be irritable and not feed, eat or drink properly
wet the bed or wet themselves
changes in behaviour, such as acting agitated or confused (delirium)
leaking pee (wetting themselves or incontinence) that is worse than usual

you try to have vaginal penetration during sex, including with a finger, sex toy or penis

a bad reaction to condoms, soap or shampoo

your eyes being uncomfortable in or sensitive to bright light
difficulty seeing at night and in low light
care_notes: Treatment for vision loss depends on what’s causing it.
If the optician or GP thinks your vision loss is caused by a condition, you’ll usually be referred to an eye specialist (ophthalmologist) for further tests.

name: Von Willebrand disease
description: Von Willebrand disease is an inherited condition where your blood does not clot properly, so you bleed more easily. There's no cure but most people have mild symptoms that can be managed.
symptom_terms: bleeding more than usual after an injury or cut
heavy bleeding that's difficult to stop, for example after an injury or procedure
pain, swelling and stiffness in a joint
care_notes: Treatment for von Willebrand disease depends on the type you have and how severe your symptoms are.
You can usually use first aid to treat less serious bleeding yourself, such as cuts and grazes or nosebleeds .

care_notes: You can buy creams, plasters and sprays from pharmacies to treat warts and verrucas.
These treatments can take up to 3 months to complete, may irritate your skin and do not always work. You should not use these treatments on your face.

pain and muscle spasms in the shoulders and arms

name: Whooping cough
description: Whooping cough (pertussis) is an infection of the lungs and breathing tubes. It spreads very easily and can be serious. It's important for babies, children and anyone who's pregnant to get vaccinated against it.
symptom_terms: will get coughing bouts that last for a few minutes and are worse at night
may make a "whoop" sound – a gasp for breath between coughs (young babies under 3 months old and some adults may not "whoop")
may have difficulty breathing after a coughing bout and may turn blue or grey (young infants)
may bring up a thick mucus, which can make you vomit
may become very red in the face (more common in adults)
care_notes: You or your child may need urgent or emergency medical help for whooping cough, depending on your symptoms.
Treatment for whooping cough depends on your age and how long you've had the infection.

name: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome
description: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome is a heart condition that can cause a very fast heartbeat. It's not usually serious but you may need treatment if symptoms are affecting your life.
symptom_terms: a fluttering feeling in your chest or your heartbeat pounding, racing or going too slowly (heart palpitations)
care_notes: Treatment for Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome depends on your symptoms and if your heart specialist (cardiologist) thinks you're at high risk of serious problems.
You might not need any treatment if you have no symptoms, or mild symptoms that only happen rarely.
